question: Describe your experience integrating React applications with REST APIs. What challenges have you encountered?
answer: At New Oriental, we built a new marking dashboard on top of the backend's REST APIs. The biggest challenge was the response data. It was deeply nested and it changed often. In plain JavaScript we kept seeing the API docs for field names, and we did typos that only showed up in QA. So I set up openapi-typescript to generate types straight from the backend's Swagger spec. We were design-first, so the spec was agreed before the endpoints were built. That meant I could build against the types while the backend team was still writing the API. Nobody wrote the API types by hand, and the editor gave us autocomplete for every field.

question: Tell me about the most challenging technical problem you've solved in a React project. What made it difficult and how did you solve it?
answer: The hardest one was the order page in our merchant console. Merchants said a competitor's console felt more responsive. I added code splitting, and LCP improved from about 3.5 seconds to 2.6, but the complaint was still there. When our team visited some merchants, I saw them run the same filter hundreds of times a day, reload the page and keep several tabs open. That's when I realised I was measuring the wrong thing. The real problem was the same request, again and again. With a senior engineer, I went through the request logs, and we used stale-while-revalidate in a Service Worker. A cached read came back in about 20 milliseconds, and the complaint went away.

question: Can you share an experience where you collaborated with cross-functional teams? What challenges did you face and how did you overcome them?
answer: At ByteDance, we built a word cloud of the top keywords in video comments. When you hovered over a keyword, a tooltip showed its numbers. Inside that tooltip, there was a second tooltip. I talked to the PM about it, because the analysts needed to compare keywords. If your mouse slips, both tooltips close, and you can't keep two open side by side. I didn't just say no. I suggested a modal, so they could read and compare the details. The PM wanted the details close to the chart, so we met in the middle: we added a 'View details' link to the tooltip, and it opened the details in a panel next to the chart. I learned to argue from the user's needs, not my own taste.

question: Explain your approach to breaking down a UI/UX design into reusable React components. What principles do you follow?
